verdicts.reasoning: Half the set hands the pupil a read-only dial (is_read_only true) and asks 'What time does the clock show?'; at seed 64 the distractors 3:50, 1:50 and 2:45 can only be eliminated by reading both hands off the face, which is the reading act itself.

Standard hour:minute notation is what the pupil has to land on, and getting it right turns on the written detail: 6:05 vs 6:00 at seed 57, 2:45 vs 2:50 at seed 64, 5:25 vs 5:30 at seed 118. Worth recording that this is recognition among four pre-written times — no sample has the pupil compose or type a time, and the five 'Set the clock' items hand the written form over in the stem rather than asking for it back.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: The writing direction appears only as answer options or as stimulus text; there is no free-entry item in these ten samples where the pupil produces the notation unaided.

verdicts.reasoning: Clock time is the sole subject matter of all ten samples, spanning 1:00 at seed 42 through 12:55 at seed 103, with each payload carrying a correct_time object naming hour and minute.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: Seeds 91 and 127 are byte-identical items ('Set the clock to show 10:00 a.m.'), so the ten samples cover only nine distinct tasks.

verdicts.reasoning: Whole-hour targets isolate the hour as the thing being judged — seed 57 keys 6:00 a.m. against 5:00 and 7:00 — and the hour hand is placed proportionally rather than snapped, e.g. hour_angle 287.5 for 9:35 at seed 11 and 165 for 5:30 at seed 118.

Six of the ten targets fall off the hour at five-minute granularity (9:35, 2:15, 2:50, 2:30, 12:55, 5:30), and minute_angle tracks them correctly — 35 min to 210 degrees, 55 min to 330 degrees — so the minute hand carries real information in those items.

Both markers are used and roughly balanced across the set: p.m. at seeds 11, 23, 42, 64 and 78; a.m. at seeds 57, 91, 103, 118 and 127. Every stem or key states the marker explicitly rather than leaving the half of the day implicit.
verdicts.content_note_from_attester: In every read item all four options share one meridiem (seed 42 is all p.m., seed 57 all a.m.), so no sample requires distinguishing a.m. from p.m. Since an analog face cannot show the meridiem, the 'p.m.' in seed 42's key is not derivable from the visual at all — it is only harmless because the distractors agree with it.

verdicts.reasoning: Every sample renders a ClockSet dial with two hands given in degrees and show_labels true — never a digital readout — and the geometry is internally consistent, e.g. seed 64's 2:50 gives hour_angle 85 and minute_angle 300, and seed 103's 12:55 gives 27.5 and 330.
